added.name: Tesser
added.long_description:
Tesser is a cloud development runtime that lets developers run multiple dev environments in parallel without overloading their laptops.

Our CLI moves workloads like servers, builds, tests, and typechecking to isolated cloud machines while developers continue using their existing editors and coding agents. Tesser handles provisioning, networking, and port forwarding. Teams can access each other's environments through our gateway, share live previews, and run Tesser on our infrastructure or their own cloud (BYOC).

long_description.before:
Trellus delivers simple coaching prompts to your salespeople in real time as they speak to prospects. Prompts are delivered in response to what is happening in a conversation. The goal of these prompts is to get more reps achieving quota and to reduce the time it takes to start attaining quota.

Prompts are action-oriented steps toward empathetic listening and effective discovery. Examples include 'pause' (when talking too much), 'set next steps' (when wrapping up a call without them), and 'ask current state' (when encountering objections).

Trellus is backed by Y Combinator and founded by former MIT researchers.
long_description.after: Trellus is a Chrome extension that power dials or parallel dials up to five lines inside the CRM or sales engagement platform a sales team already uses, and saves each call's outcome, notes and callback back to the record the rep called from. Reps rehearse objections with AI practice calls, and teams on the Business plan add real-time AI coaching, team analytics and a virtual sales floor. Plans start at $99.99 per seat per month.

one_liner.after: Power and parallel dialing with AI coaching, inside your CRM

long_description.before:
Ellipsis is a cloud platform that allows engineering teams to deploy fleets of coding agents. Each agent gets an isolated sandbox, scoped permissions, and hard budget caps. Full observability included. Get started with a $100 credit at www.ellipsis.dev.

You can deploy agents for feature development, code review, and workflow automation. Creating an agent is simple: simply commit a YAML file to Github. Spawn agents from Github/Linear/Slack/etc., or via a REST API or our CLI. 

Organizations get full observability and governance of their cloud coding agents.  Agent session logs are downloadable so companies own their own data.

Full documentation: https://www.ellipsis.dev/docs
long_description.after:
Ellipsis is a Managed Agent Platform for Developers. Spawn, manage, and govern cloud agents for Software Factories, custom Code Review, and Background Tasks. You choose the model, harness, prompts, and tools. We'll handle the infrastructure.

Documentation: https://www.ellipsis.dev/docs

long_description.before:
Carma is building an AI-native platform that transforms fleet operations from tedious, manual work into effortless, automated workflows.

We’re the fastest-growing company in fleet management software. Carma already powers some of the largest fleets in the U.S., saving operations teams thousands of hours by eliminating busywork and keeping vehicles on the road.

Backed by Soma Capital, Y Combinator, founders of Superhuman, and Tier-1 investors, we are sprinting toward a Series A in 2026.

We’re hiring the top 0.1% of engineers who want real ownership and impact—starting Day 1, you’ll build and ship fast to production for enterprise clients. Fleet operations run in real time, so your work is immediately used in the field and gets real customer feedback in hours, not months.
long_description.after:
Carma is the agentic workspace that runs construction operations for profit.

Our customers are the $100M+ contractors building America’s data centers.

The AGI race is a construction race. More than 40% of America’s 2026 data centers are late, and every month of delay is a gift to the CCP. They’re late because contractors still coordinate every jobsite by phone and spreadsheet.

Contractors sell their work at fixed prices, so every hour a crew waits comes out of their margin. One broken machine stops every crew behind it, and the repair invoice shows only a fraction of the cost. The rest lands in idle crews and higher bids on the next job.

Adam, our AI operator, runs equipment operations for the whole company’s profit. He prices every idle hour, picks the repair with the lowest total cost, audits every bill before it’s paid, reallocates idle machines to the jobs that need them, and tells the company which machines to buy, repair, or sell. Managers approve every cost and Adam handles the coordination in between.

In three months, Adam increased operating profit by $4.21M a year for a $500M electrical contracting customer: a 12% increase. Across customers, the time people spend coordinating each repair fell 93%, and equipment downtime fell 30%.

We crossed $2M ARR three months after our first invoice, with five enterprise customers and a five-person team. Customers pay annually upfront, so we’re cash-flow positive. Carma sells no parts, rentals, or machines, so Adam’s only incentive is our customer’s profit.

Whoever builds faster wins. We will make sure it’s America.

one_liner.before: The AI Operating System For Modern Fleets.
one_liner.after: The agentic workspace that runs construction operations for profit

long_description.before:
Amika is infra to build your software factory.

We give your team sandboxed AI coding agents in the cloud: the same infrastructure Ramp, Coinbase, and Stripe built in-house. Kick off work from a web UI, CLI, Slack, or API. Use your preferred coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, etc.). Each agent understands your codebase, runs autonomously, and ships real PRs with live previews of the apps it changed. Use it as your daily driver or plug it into your own code-gen pipeline via API.
long_description.after:
Amika slices computers you already own (a spare Mac Mini, a desktop, EC2 in your VPC) into isolated agent devboxes or CI runners, and puts them all on one private network you can reach from anywhere.

Use Amika to give your agents always-on computers, to offload CI and build to your own machines, or for anything else where you want to run software and agents on your own devices.

one_liner.before: Infra to build your own software factory
one_liner.after: Turn any spare computer into agent devboxes or CI runners
